question.text: The line $y=m x$ bisects the area unclosed by lines $x=0, y=0$ and $x=\frac{3}{2}$ and the curve $y=1+4 x-x^2$. Then, the value of $m$ is

solution.text: Given, $y=1+4 x-x^2$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=4-2 x=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \text{[point of maxima]}\\ & \Rightarrow \quad y_{\max }=1+4 \times 2-4=5 \end{aligned}$ when, $x=0, y=1$ $\therefore$ Graph according to question and above information $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \text { If } y=m x \text { bisects the area bounded } \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A_1=A_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \int_0^{3 / 2}\left(1+4 x-x^2\right) d x=2 \int_0^{3 / 2} m x d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left[x+2 x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{3 / 2}=\left[m x^2\right]_0^{3 / 2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}+2 \times \frac{9}{4}-\frac{27}{8} \times \frac{1}{3}=m \times \frac{9}{4} \\ & \therefore \quad m=\frac{13}{6}\end{aligned}$
